items.title: Google Photos is forcing some Galaxy users to save every minor edit as a copy
items.summary:
TL;DR 

Google Photos is forcing some Samsung Galaxy users running One UI 9 to save even minor edits as separate copies. 
 We’ve independently confirmed the absence of the regular Save option on a Galaxy S23 FE. 
 Samsung has reportedly escalated the issue to its engineers, though it’s still unclear whether this is a bug or an intentional change. 

Google Photos is forcing some Samsung Galaxy users to save images with simple edits, like minor crops, as their own copies. As you might expect, this is already causing frustration among users who are now stuck deleting unnecessary copies from their Google Photos libraries every time they make a minor adjustment to an image.

For reference, the app has traditionally allowed users to simply overwrite original images after minor edits have been made to them. The tech giant recently went as far as letting users overwrite original images even after advanced edits like Magic Eraser, Unblur, or edits with UltraHDR and C2PA formats. That’s precisely why the sudden disappearance of the regular Save option for basic edits is perplexing.
items.t: Google Photos is forcing some Galaxy users to save every minor edit as a copy

items.title: Google Messages is preparing iMessage-style threaded replies to make chats easier to follow
items.summary:
TL;DR 

Google Messages is working on iMessage-style threaded replies to make it easier to follow multiple discussions within a single conversation. 
 The feature uses visual connectors, reply counters, and a dedicated thread view that isolates related messages and lets users reply directly within a thread. 
 We were able to enable threaded replies in both individual and RCS group conversations. The feature isn’t publicly available yet. 

Google Messages is ready to take yet another page out of Apple’s iMessage playbook with threaded replies, and the similarities are hard to overlook. Individual conversations and group chats aren’t necessarily seamless to follow with Google Messages’ current message reply implementation, especially when you’re talking about multiple topics simultaneously. Threaded replies, as we’ve seen in other apps, can easily alleviate some of the confusion.

Currently, when you reply to a message on Google Messages, the app simply attaches a preview of the original message right above your response. The app does this for all subsequent replies to the original message and its associated responses. This works when you’re sending through a one-off reply, but it doesn’t work when you’re trying to follow a back-and-forth conversation that might have stemmed from one single message.
items.t: Google Messages is preparing iMessage-style threaded replies to make chats easier to follow

items.title: Your old smartphone is likely worth more now as a trade-in than it was last year
items.summary:
Credit: Robert Triggs / Android Authority 

TL;DR 

A new report has found that phone trade-in activity has declined year over year in the US. 
 At the same time, trade-in values have increased significantly. 
 The average trade-in value rose 27% for Android phones and 18% for iPhones. 

When it’s time to purchase a new phone, do you take advantage of the trade-in deals ? While your old phone could help you save money on your next handset, there are reasons why you may want to keep your old device. It appears more people are choosing to keep their old hardware these days, and in turn, that mindset is driving up the value of trade-ins.

According to a report from Assurant , fewer smartphones in the US were traded in during Q3 2026 than in the same time frame last year. This is reportedly the first year since 2017 that money returned through trade-in programs declined year over year, excluding the pandemic. Specifically, $1.53 billion was returned in Q3 2026, shrinking from $1.59 billion in 2025.
items.t: Your old smartphone is likely worth more now as a trade-in than it was last year

items.title: Google Home bug is cluttering device lists with redundant tiles

 The issue affects devices from multiple manufacturers, including TP-Link Kasa and Leviton, and extends to the Google Home widget. 
 The bug’s underlying cause remains unclear, and unlinking and relinking affected devices doesn’t appear to resolve the issue. 

Google Home ‘s latest bug has some users seeing double — literally. A new glitch is currently causing users’ smart home devices to show up twice within the Google Home app, with one tile identifying the device for what it is and the other identifying it as an outlet or a wall switch.

The bug first showed up early in November, though affected users report that it is still prevalent . It doesn’t discriminate — the issue appears to affect devices from multiple manufacturers, with users indicating that the devices show up correctly within their respective companion apps. This confirms that the bug stems from Google Home and not the hardware.

items.title: Motorola Razr 2027 leak suggests a January launch is in the cards
items.summary:
Credit: Stephen Radochia / Android Authority 

TL;DR 

A new report says Motorola is planning to launch the Razr 2027 in January. 
 The base model will reportedly adopt the 4-inch cover display featured on the Plus and Ultra. 
 The cover screen’s refresh rate on the base model has been raised from 90Hz to 120Hz. 

With November almost done, there’s only one more month separating us from CES. The January event should be packed to the gills with plenty of surprises. According to a new leak, one of those surprises may be the launch of the Motorola Razr 2027.

Android Headlines reports that Motorola is eyeing early January as a launch date for the Razr 2027 series. Motorola is expected to be a part of Lenovo’s Tech World event at CES, which will be held on January 6. The leak suggests that the Razr announcement could be made during this event. If true, this would move up the launch timeline by a couple of months, as the Razr 2026 was released in May.

items.title: HUAWEI’s new Watch Air is slimmer and lighter than any Pixel Watch or Galaxy Watch ever
items.summary:
Credit: HUAWEI 

TL;DR 

HUAWEI has launched its Watch Air, which is thinner than most modern smartwatches. 
 The Watch Air is only 6.9mm thick and weighs just 29 grams. 
 It runs HarmonyOS 2.0 and works with both Android and iOS. 

HUAWEI might have been forced to stop selling its devices in the US, along with most of the world, but that hasn’t stopped it from pushing the limits of innovation. Earlier today, the company announced its latest foldable, the Mate X8 , with an eye-searingly bright display and a promise that the hinge will last 700,000 folds. The phone even uses levitating magnets under the screen to reduce strain on the folding screen and limit creasing. Another selling point of the Mate X8 is that it’s the slimmest foldable on the market, measuring just 4.2mm when unfolded. To complement the sleek foldable, HUAWEI has also announced a smartwatch significantly slimmer than the latest Pixel or Galaxy Watch devices.

Called the HUAWEI Watch Air, the smartwatch measures only 6.9mm in thickness, excluding the sensor area, and weighs just 27 grams. The Apple Watch inspiration is uncanny, with a rotating crown that doubles as a pressable button along with a flat function button. HUAWEI doubles down by draping the Watch Air in titanium alloy-based finishes. It comes in six color options, including Phantom Night Black, Phantom Silver, Gilded Gold, Floating White, Nebula Apricot, and Spruce Green.
items.t: HUAWEI’s new Watch Air is slimmer and lighter than any Pixel Watch or Galaxy Watch ever

Motorola unveiled the Edge 70 Neo yesterday and today announced its pricing and availability. The smartphone comes in a single 8GB/128GB configuration, priced at INR40,999. However, for a limited period, it will be available at INR37,999.

The Edge 70 Neo will go on sale in India starting December 1 through Motorola's Indian website, Flipkart, and leading retail stores, including Reliance Digital. Customers have four color options: Pantone Mountain View, Pantone Milky Blue, Pantone Sage, and Pantone Gray Lilac.

items.title: Huawei Mate 90 Air arrives with familiar specs
items.summary:
As expected, Huawei announced its Mate 90 Air in China today. The device is the successor to last year’s Mate 70 Air and you’d expect to see some upgrades across its specs, but that’s mostly not the case here.

Huawei Mate 90 Air

Mate 90 Air retains the same core specs as the Mate 70 Air while introducing a new back design and a 0.02mm thinner chassis. There's a new Rose Gold color option, which joins the Bright Moon Silver and Obsidian Black hues.

Outside of the minor cosmetic changes, the Mate 90 Air is basically a repackaged Mate 70 Air. It’s built around the same 7-inch LTPO...

items.title: Honor Magic9 Pro Max begins its global rollout with Malaysia
items.summary:
Honor just kicked off the global rollout of its Honor Magic9 Pro Max, which was first announced in China. European consumers will have to wait until January, but Asian markets like Malaysia are already receiving the first units.

While most of the hardware remains the same, some memory configurations won't make it outside of China, and the battery capacity is slightly lower.

The available memory configurations globally are 12GB/256GB, 12GB/512GB and 16GB/1TB, while the battery capacity is confirmed to be 8,000 mAh, which is 800 mAh less than the Chinese version. As for color...

items.title: Nothing's upcoming AI device is a pair of earbuds called the Ear (note)
items.summary:
Nothing is set to launch its first AI-native product on December 8. Ahead of the launch, the company has revealed that the product is a pair of earbuds called the Ear (note), which can record and transcribe calls and meetings using AI.

Bloomberg's Mark Gurman spoke with Nothing co-founder Carl Pei, who gave the publication a first look at the product.

According to the publication, the Ear (note) will use microphones on both the earbuds and the charging case to record and transcribe conversations. The case can be used to record in-person meetings or classes, while the earbuds can...
items.t: Nothing's upcoming AI device is a pair of earbuds called the Ear (note)

items.title: WhatsApp's 'View Once' text messages feature is now available to beta users on iOS
items.summary:
About two weeks ago, we learned that WhatsApp's "View Once" feature for text messages was available to beta users on Android. WABetaInfo reports it's now available to some users on beta version 26.45.10.73 of WhatsApp for iOS.

WhatsApp's view-once feature for text messages on iOS works the same way as on Android. Type the text in the box, press and hold the send button, then select "View Once." WhatsApp shows information about view-once texts the first time you use it. Click "OK" to proceed.

The recipient must tap the view-once text in the chat to read it, and it opens in a separate...
items.t: WhatsApp's 'View Once' text messages feature is now available to beta users on iOS

items.title: Honor's first wide foldable set to arrive in March 2027 with zero-crease display
items.summary:
At the recent Honor 700 series launch event, the company reportedly shared details about its first wide foldable. Honor CEO Li Jian also confirmed the phone's expected launch window.

Li Jian reportedly said the wide foldable will debut in March 2027. He also claimed that Honor has made new breakthroughs in foldable display technology.

Honor Magic V6

According to the CEO, the upcoming phone will feature a crease-free display. He reportedly also urged consumers considering the Apple iPhone Duo to wait and try Honor's alternative.

items.title: Motorola officially announces when the Signature 27 is coming to India
items.summary:
Motorola semi-announced the Signature 27 back in September and made it fully official earlier this month, with sales in Europe starting on November 16. In October, the company's Indian website said the phone was "coming this November", but that turned out to be a bit optimistic.
